title: Hearing and Meeting Transcription with Minutes
summary: Transcribe arbitral hearings, depositions and client meetings where recording is permitted, label speakers, handle Hindi-English speech and legal terms, and draft minutes for review.

seo.title: Hearing and Meeting Transcription with Minutes | VipraTech
seo.description: AI transcription for arbitral hearings and legal meetings with speaker labels, legal vocabulary, Hindi-English support and draft minutes for review.

problem.intro: Ad hoc arbitrations in India often run without a professional stenographer, and lawyers and tribunal secretaries reconstruct proceedings from handwritten notes. Client conferences, witness preparation sessions and internal case meetings produce decisions and action items that live only in someone's notebook.

pain_points.title: No reliable record
pain_points.detail: Without a transcript, disputes about what a witness said or what the tribunal directed are hard to settle.

pain_points.title: Generic transcription fails
pain_points.detail: Case names, statutory references, Latin terms and Hindi-English switching produce garbled output from consumer tools.

pain_points.title: Speakers not identified
pain_points.detail: A transcript that does not say who spoke, whether counsel, witness or arbitrator, is of limited use.

pain_points.title: Minutes take hours
pain_points.detail: Turning a long hearing or meeting into minutes, procedural notes and action items takes associate time after a full day.

solution.overview: We build a transcription and minutes pipeline for proceedings where recording is permitted: arbitral hearings, depositions, virtual hearings with the tribunal's approval, and client or internal meetings with participants' consent. Audio from the hearing room or a video-conference platform is split by speaker and mapped to named participants, then transcribed with a glossary built from the matter, including party names, case citations and statutes, across Hindi, English and mixed speech. Low-confidence segments are marked for a transcript reviewer who checks them against the audio. From the reviewed transcript the system drafts minutes, a summary of directions and action items, which counsel or the tribunal secretary approve before circulation.
capabilities: Speaker separation mapped to named counsel, witnesses and arbitrators
Matter-specific glossary for parties, citations, statutes and technical terms
Hindi, English and code-switched transcription with time stamps
Low-confidence segments marked for review against the audio
Draft minutes, directions summary and action items from the reviewed transcript
Errata workflow for parties to propose corrections

workflow.title: Confirm permission and capture
workflow.detail: Recording proceeds only with the tribunal's or participants' permission, from room microphones or the video-conference platform.

workflow.title: Separate and label speakers
workflow.detail: Speech is split by speaker and mapped to the names on the appearance list.

workflow.title: Transcribe with the glossary
workflow.detail: Audio is transcribed using the matter glossary, with time stamps and a confidence score for each segment.

workflow.title: Review uncertain segments
workflow.detail: A transcript reviewer corrects marked segments against the audio.

workflow.title: Draft minutes
workflow.detail: Minutes, directions and action items are drafted from the reviewed transcript.

workflow.title: Approve and circulate
workflow.detail: Counsel or the tribunal secretary approve the documents, and parties can submit errata.

inputs: Audio or video of the hearing or meeting
Matter glossary: parties, citations, statutes and technical terms
Agenda or procedural order, if any
outputs: List of corrected segments and errata
Action items with owners and dates
Approved, versioned records in matter storage
human_in_the_loop: A transcript reviewer checks every low-confidence segment against the audio, and counsel or the tribunal secretary approve the minutes before circulation. Parties can propose errata, which the approver decides.
integrations: Zoom, Microsoft Teams or Google Meet recordings
Microsoft Word for transcripts and minutes
guardrails: No recording without tribunal or participant permission, and no recording of court proceedings
Uncertain words marked, never silently filled in
Minutes drafted only from the reviewed transcript
Recordings and transcripts restricted to the matter team and kept for the agreed period
Audio and transcripts not used to train models
compliance_notes: Courts in India generally restrict recording of proceedings without permission; this service is designed for arbitral hearings, depositions and meetings where recording is agreed.
Recordings contain participants' personal data; consent and retention are handled in line with the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: Two or three recorded arbitral sessions or internal meetings, with transcripts reviewed against the audio by your team.
deliverables: Reviewed transcripts for the pilot sessions
Accuracy report by speaker and language

what_we_measure.how: Reviewed transcript compared with the raw output, by language and speaker.
Segments assigned to the correct speaker, from reviewer corrections.

what_we_measure.metric: Reviewer time per hour of audio
what_we_measure.how: Time the reviewer spends correcting each recorded hour.
Extent of the changes the approver made to the draft minutes.

faqs.a: We do not record court proceedings, which courts generally restrict without permission. The service is for arbitral hearings, depositions, virtual hearings where the tribunal permits recording, and meetings where participants agree.

faqs.q: How accurate is it with Hindi and legal terms?
faqs.a: Accuracy improves with a matter glossary and good audio. Every low-confidence segment is marked for review, and the pilot reports error rates by language and speaker.
The client or tribunal, as agreed for the proceeding. We keep it in matter-restricted storage and delete it at the end of the agreed period.

faqs.q: Can the minutes include the tribunal's directions?
faqs.a: Yes. The drafter pulls directions and deadlines from the reviewed transcript into a summary, which counsel or the tribunal secretary approve.
